subject: Biology
title: How Big Is a Cell?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How Big Is a Cell?.

hook.text: Most human cells are about 10 micrometers wide. A hundred could line up on one millimeter.

buildup.text: Bacteria are ten times smaller. Viruses are smaller still—invisible to light microscopes.

discovery.text: The largest single cell? An ostrich egg, about 15 centimeters across.

twist.text: Some nerve cells stretch over a meter long, running from your spine to your toes.

climax.text: Size shapes function. Small cells exchange materials fast; large cells store more.

punchline.text: Life works at scales you can barely imagine.

quiz.question: What is the largest single cell?

details.summary: Most human cells range from 10 to 100 micrometers in diameter, invisible to the naked eye. Cell size is constrained by the surface-area-to-volume ratio: cells must be small enough for nutrients and waste to diffuse efficiently across their membranes.
details.whyItMatters: Cell size limits explain why organisms grow by adding more cells rather than making bigger ones. This constraint shapes everything from tissue architecture to why single-celled organisms cannot become visible without special adaptations.
takeaways: Most human cells are 10 to 100 micrometers, requiring microscopes to see
Surface-area-to-volume ratio limits how large cells can grow
Red blood cells are about 8 micrometers; neurons can extend over a meter

faq.question: Why can't cells just keep getting bigger?
faq.answer: As a cell grows, its volume increases faster than its surface area. Eventually the membrane cannot import enough nutrients or export enough waste to sustain the interior. This is why large organisms have trillions of small cells rather than a few giant ones.

faq.question: What is the largest single cell?
faq.answer: The ostrich egg is the largest single cell, measuring about 15 centimeters. Among human cells, a motor neuron's axon can stretch over a meter from the spinal cord to the foot, though its cell body is microscopic.
